articles.title: Do spiders dream? Researchers studying Australian jumping spiders have found sleep patterns resembling REM sleep, raising new questions about dream-like states in invertebrates
articles.summary: Dreaming is an experience we often associate with humans but is it something that only humans experience?
articles.body: Dreaming is an experience we often associate with humans but is it something that only humans experience? Scientists have long been curious to ascertain what may happen when other animals fall asleep. While certain sleep behaviours have been observed in mammals and birds, much less is known about how sleep works in creatures with a distinct nervous system. Researchers at the University of Bonn have studied the Australian jumping spider, Portia fimbriata, known to be a clever hunter. As Science Daily reported on the 27th of October 2026, researchers have discovered evidence of distinct sleep stages, including one that resembles the rapid eye movement (REM) sleep seen in humans, opening up new questions about whether spiders could experience something resembling dreams.The study, conducted by researchers at the University of Bonn in Germany, examined the Australian jumping spider Portia fimbriata. The findings, published in the journal Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, by monitoring the spiders on several days and nights found clear evidence that spiders experience regulated sleep, and a REM-like sleep that is “marked by eye movements and muscle twitches” .The observations also suggest that some features of sleep may be shared by animals separated by considerable evolutionary differences.A research study: Portia fimbriata The choice of spider is particularly interesting because Portia fimbriata is known for its sophisticated hunting behaviour. Members of the genus Portia prey on other spiders and use different strategies to approach and capture them which include imitating the vibrations of insects struggling in a webb, that can draw another spider towards what appears to be potential prey.Such behaviour has made these spiders interesting subjects for researchers investigating animal learning and cognition. Their hunting strategies also raise questions about how their nervous systems support complex behaviour, making their sleep patterns another avenue for scientific investigation. Although scientists have previously reported REM-like movements in jumping spiders, establishing whether these movements occur during genuine sleep required further investigation. The latest study set out to examine not only the movements themselves but also whether the spiders showed other behavioural signs associated with sleep.What happens when spiders fall asleep?To observe the spiders, the researchers recorded their behaviour over several days and nights, using infrared cameras to monitor them in darkness. Each individual Portia fimbriata spider was placed in the plastic dishes measuring 12 centimeters in diameter. The animal was also monitored in different lighting conditions to examine distinguishable sleeping stages. The infrared camera helped monitor and reveal their distinct sleeping stages, The recordings revealed two distinguishable sleep stages, including a period of quiet rest followed by a stage marked by eye movements and muscle twitches, however this response does not necessarily mean that these animals experience the same REM sleep like humans.These movements are particularly noteworthy because rapid eye movements and changes in muscle activity are associated with REM sleep in humans and other vertebrates. The similarities prompted researchers to investigate whether the spiders' behaviour represented a distinct stage of sleep rather than ordinary inactivity.However, the resemblance does not establish that spiders dream. The researchers relied on behavioural observations rather than direct examination of their brain activity, meaning they could not determine whether the spiders experienced dreams or what might occur in their brains during these periods.The team also tested how readily the spiders responded to sound to test whether they were asleep or just lay motionless. During the observed sleep stages, their responses to disturbances were delayed compared with when they were awake, and some spiders did not respond at all. Researchers additionally investigated "sleep rebound", a phenomenon in which an animal makes up for disrupted sleep afterwards. Together, these observations provided evidence that the spiders experience regulated sleep with distinct stages, strengthening the case that their nighttime behaviour involves more than simply resting.Can spiders dream then? Sciene Daily has come to note that while the Bonn University is in the process of expanding its research, what remains to be explored is the relationship between sleep and cognitive abilties. However, what the research does tell us is that creatures that are seemingly small and jumpy can have complex sleeping systems just like us humans.Whether spiders can dream or not still remains to be know, but the ongoing inquiry and isnghts into the spiders night time behavouir and responses to external factors has offered a way for understandign how widley different features are distributed across the animal kingdom, with the research time likely to expand the inquiry into how animals sleep in their natural environments.

articles.title: Here’s Virgin Galactic’s new Apeiron spaceship
articles.summary: Virgin Galactic unveiled its new Apeiron spacecraft, which is now expected to launch in Q2 2027.
articles.body: Virgin Galactic’s new spaceship is here, dubbed “Apeiron” by popular vote from a public poll. Apeiron is the first of the company’s new Delta-class spacecraft, but it isn’t slated to launch for nearly another year. Earlier this week, Virgin Galactic announced another delay in its launch timeline: > The lead Spaceship’s first commercial spaceflight is now expected in early Q2 2027, and the second Spaceship is expected to begin commercial spaceflight operations in late Q2/early Q3 2027. The updated timeline reflects additional time for completing avionics software integration and validation, which uses an exhaustive testing process. That testing will conclude at Spaceport America as the lead Spaceship is readied for its flight test series. [Media: Virgin Galactic had previously delayed its next commercial spaceflight to February 2027, rather than late 2026. It’s now been over two years since Virgin Galactic’s last commercial spaceflight in June 2024, when it retired its VSS Unity spacecraft. Apeiron is leaving Virgin Galactic’s Mesa, Arizona Spaceship Factory on Wednesday onboard a captive-carry flight with its Eve launch vehicle, heading to Spaceport America in New Mexico, where Virgin Galactic says its “engineering team plans to complete avionics software validation before beginning flight tests.”

articles.title: A Minnesota farmer harvesting corn found a mysterious 11-foot-wide metallic object in his field; space experts now suspect it is debris from a Chinese rocket launched in September, but its origin remains unconfirmed
articles.summary: On the afternoon of 14 October, a farmer in Scott Township, Stevens County, western Minnesota, was walking through his cornfield when he stumbled upon
articles.body: On the afternoon of 14 October, a farmer in Scott Township, Stevens County, western Minnesota, was walking through his cornfield when he stumbled upon something that did not belong there. The metal was charred and round, about 11 feet across. He couldn’t say what it was, so he dialled the sheriff’s office. The deputies who went out to look agreed: it was unusual. It looked like the premise of Steven Spielberg’s latest UFO blockbuster flick. All they knew was that it was not farm equipment.What is the mysterious object?In a press release from the sheriff’s office, officials described it as “a large metallic object”. They said the object was “presumably a space object”. State and federal agencies were called in to investigate the debris and help remove it from the property. “Agency officials have determined that there is no danger to the public due to this incident,” the sheriff’s office assured the public. But the pressing questions remained: what was the object, and where did it come from?The object may have lain in the field for about six weeks, through the growing season and into harvest, local outlets, including the Rapid City Post and NBC affiliates KARE 11 and 9News, reported. Either way, no one knew it was there until the farmer found it. Scott Township is home to about 117 people, which helps explain how something of this size could go unnoticed.This information has led some experts to suspect that the debris may have come from a rocket. The metal matches the upper stage of a Zhuque-2E, a rocket built by the Chinese company LandSpace. It lifted off on 15 September from north-western China with 10 satellites for the Qianfan network, a project intended to rival SpaceX’s Starlink. That same night, people in Kansas, Minnesota and Wisconsin filmed fireballs crossing the sky. Ars Technica has linked those videos to the rocket.The measurements are the strongest clue. The upper stage is about 3.35 metres across, close to the 11 feet reported in the field. Some reports suggest that the metal could be the end cap of a fuel tank. That is a useful description, but it is not yet a confirmed identification.Under the 1972 Space Liability Convention, the country that launches a space object is liable for any damage it causes on Earth.This incident is not the first of its kind. Over the years, similar debris has turned up in other places. In July, metal spheres washed ashore in Australia and were traced to a launch vehicle. In Indonesia, a large metal object found in a palm oil plantation is also being investigated as a possible Zhuque-2E fragment. Reports say the same rocket’s upper stage broke apart in orbit during an earlier flight in June.Meanwhile, official confirmation of the identity of this unusual metallic object found on a Minnesota farm is still pending. The sheriff’s office says investigators are working to determine the object’s origin.

articles.title: Trump DOE loans $5B to nuclear plants that will power data centers | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Constellation Energy will get $5 billion in government loans to modernize nuclear reactors. Most of the new capacity is already committed to Google, Amazon, and Meta.
articles.body:
The Trump administration is giving Constellation Energy $5 billion in loans to expand nuclear generating capacity at eight power plants by 1.1 gigawatts.

Most or all of the additional power from seven of those facilities has already been bought by Google, Meta, or Amazon.

Constellation said it plans to use the financing to “uprate” 11 existing reactors, an industry term for expanding capacity at a reactor, often by using more highly enriched uranium and by upgrading equipment to handle the increased power levels.

The energy company said it had already committed to spending more than $7 billion to add 1,080 megawatts of nuclear capacity to deliver power to Google, Amazon, and Meta. The loan commitment, which has yet to be finalized, “could lower financing costs” for the projects, Constellation said in a press release .

The eight power plants include six in Illinois (Braidwood, Byron, Clinton, Dresden, LaSalle, and Quad Cities), one in Maryland (Calvert Cliffs), and one in Pennsylvania (Limerick).

Google is already the confirmed buyer of additional power from the Pennsylvania plant and four Illinois power plants, while Amazon is buying electricity from the Maryland plant and Meta is effectively buying the entire Clinton power plant in Illinois.

On Tuesday, the Department of Energy touted the loan as supporting “affordable, reliable power to American homes and businesses,” though there is no evidence that the new nuclear capacity will lower prices for residential ratepayers. Constellation’s announcement does not say whether the projects will maintain or lower electricity rates, and the company would not confirm the government’s claim to TechCrunch.

Hyperscalers, including Google, Amazon, and Meta, have been scouring the grid for additional capacity to support their AI data centers. Tech companies are paying handsomely for energy, committing tens of billions of dollars over the coming years. Given that power has become a competitive advantage, that estimate is probably on the low end.

By lowering the cost of capital for the upgrades, the Department of Energy’s loans could boost Constellation’s bottom line, that of the hyperscalers — or both.

articles.title: Scientists have discovered a giant new fungus in China that grows up to 20 inches tall and weighs nearly five pounds, making it the largest known of its kind and a surprising new find in a well-studied group
articles.summary: Hidden among the roots of trees in China’s lush forests, an extraordinary organism has emerged as a reminder that nature still has plenty of surprises in
articles.body: Hidden among the roots of trees in China’s lush forests, an extraordinary organism has emerged as a reminder that nature still has plenty of surprises in store. Rising nearly 20 inches above the forest floor and weighing close to five pounds, the newly identified fungus is challenging scientists’ understanding of how large certain fungal structures can become. Its remarkable dimensions are not its only distinction: genetic evidence suggests its evolutionary lineage dates back approximately 65 million years. Scroll down to read the details.Meet D-rex, the fungal giantNamed Dianjunus rex and nicknamed D-rex, the species was discovered during surveys of forest environments in Yunnan province, southwestern China. According to ScienceDaily, researchers from the Kunming Institute of Botany encountered unusual whitish structures growing from the woody roots of Chinese cork oak trees.These structures, known as stromata, are reproductive formations that produce spores. Reaching approximately 50 centimetres in height and weighing up to 2.2 kilograms, they are the largest known fruiting bodies among fungi belonging to the phylum Ascomycota.As reported by People, previously known fruiting bodies in this group generally reached considerably smaller heights, making D-rex an exceptional discovery even within a major fungal group comprising tens of thousands of recognised species.A new branch on the fungal family treeThe scientists initially suspected they had encountered an unfamiliar fungus. However, laboratory investigations revealed something more significant. By examining its physical characteristics, cultivating its spores and analysing its DNA, the team established that the organism was sufficiently distinct to warrant an entirely new genus and family, Dianjunaceae.ScienceDaily reports that D-rex belongs to the order Xylariales, a group known for producing specialised compounds and enzymes that help break down complex plant material. Researchers believe the newly identified fungus may similarly obtain nutrients by decomposing dead wood, although its precise ecological role requires further investigation.An evolutionary link to the age of dinosaursPerhaps the most intriguing aspect of the discovery lies in its ancient origins. Using molecular-clock analysis, researchers compared the fungus’s genetic information with that of hundreds of other fungal species to estimate when its lineage first emerged.The findings suggest that Dianjunaceae originated around 65 million years ago, approximately one million years after the Cretaceous-Paleogene mass extinction that wiped out non-avian dinosaurs.According to People, this timeline has prompted researchers to consider whether the environmental upheaval following the extinction created new opportunities for wood-decomposing fungi. Changes in forest ecosystems and the availability of dead plant material may have helped ancestral fungi diversify.Why does it grow so large?According to ScienceDaily, scientists are still investigating what enabled D-rex to develop such towering reproductive structures. One possibility is that its height improves spore dispersal, allowing spores to catch air currents above vegetation and debris on the forest floor.However, producing such a large structure requires considerable energy. Its unusual size may therefore represent an evolutionary advantage in particular forest conditions rather than a strategy that would benefit every fungus.More discoveries could be waitingThe finding also highlights the remarkable biodiversity of East Asian forests, where varied habitats and complex ecological relationships support unusual organisms. As ScienceDaily notes, difficult terrain, seasonal growth patterns and the often-hidden nature of fungi have made many species challenging to document.Further exploration may reveal more unexpected fungal forms, offering scientists fresh insights into evolution, forest ecosystems and the extraordinary diversity of life that remains undiscovered.Image Courtesy: Kunming Institute of Botany / Chinese Academy of Sciences
